title: perf-bench-scratch-maria-gonzalez-2026-03-19
content:
Goal:
- Quick scratchpad for latency/throughput runs comparing kv-cache behavior, batching, and sequence length impact on 13B chat model (quantized).

Environment:
- Cluster: dedicated A100 80GB nodes (single GPU per worker)
- Runtime: inference-runtime v0.9.2 (kernel selection enabled)
- Model: llama-2-13b-chat (GPT-style causal), q4_k_m quantization
- Tokenizer: sentencepiece (avg token length ~= 4.1 chars)
- Requests: synthetic prompts derived from product prompt sets (helpdesk / short convo starter / long context)
- Measurement tooling: perf-client v1.3 (reports p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/s, errors)

Experiment matrix:
- Sequence lengths: 64 (short), 256 (medium), 1024 (long)
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16
- KV cache: cold (no cache), warm (same user prefix repeated), prefix_cache enabled/disabled
- Concurrency: ramp-up until 95% GPU utilization or error rate >2%

Raw results summary (representative single-run averages):
- Short seq (64 tokens)
  - BS=1: throughput = 18 req/s, p95 latency = 85 ms, p99 = 140 ms
  - BS=4: throughput = 62 req/s, p95 = 140 ms, p99 = 260 ms
  - BS=8: throughput = 110 req/s, p95 = 270 ms, p99 = 480 ms
  - BS=16: throughput = 150 req/s, p95 = 520 ms, p99 = 900 ms
  Observations: batching increases tokens/sec but p95/p99 blow up for short seq once batching >4 due to marginal queueing overhead dominating small decode time.

- Medium seq (256 tokens)
  - BS=1: throughput = 6.5 req/s, p95 = 320 ms, p99 = 480 ms
  - BS=4: throughput = 22 req/s, p95 = 540 ms, p99 = 900 ms
  - BS=8: throughput = 38 req/s, p95 = 960 ms, p99 = 1.6 s
  - BS=16: throughput = 55 req/s, p95 = 1.9 s, p99 = 3.2 s
  Observations: batching yields good tokens/sec but latency SLOs degrade; sweet spot for latency-sensitive medium workloads seems BS=1-4.

- Long seq (1024 tokens)
  - BS=1: throughput = 1.5 req/s, p95 = 1.8 s, p99 = 3.0 s
  - BS=4: throughput = 5.6 req/s, p95 = 3.9 s, p99 = 6.2 s
  - BS=8: throughput = 9.6 req/s, p95 = 7.2 s, p99 = 12.1 s
  Observations: long sequences are dominated by decode cost; batching helps amortize but tail grows nonlinearly.

KV cache / prefix caching micro-experiments (medium prompts with repeated prefixes):
- Cold vs warm (no prefix cache)
  - Cold (first request): BS=1: p95=340 ms
  - Warm (same prefix repeated, KV cached): BS=1: p95=120 ms (approx 2.8x improvement)
- Prefix cache (server-side prefix caching enabled)
  - Warm + prefix_cache: p95=95 ms, p99=150 ms (adds small memory overhead but huge improvement for repeated prompts).
Notes: prefix_cache benefits workloads with repeated system/user prefixes (for example support templates); for diverse prompts, cache hit rate drops and benefit disappears.

Batching latency breakdown (short seq, BS=8):
- Queueing: ~60% of added latency compared to BS=1 (requests wait to form batch)
- Decoding: ~30% improvement per token compared to BS=1 (due to kernel efficiency)
- Serialization/overhead: ~10%

Resource utilization notes:
- GPU occupancy >80% required to hit high tokens/sec for long seqs; kernel selection tuned to model dims gave 10-12% ops improvement vs baseline.
- Memory pressure: prefix_cache enabled increases GPU memory ~6-8% per cached prefix on 13B. Watch for OOM on higher concurrency.

Quick conclusions / heuristics:
- For latency-sensitive (p95 < 300ms) features with short responses: prefer BS=1-4, enable KV warm cache where applicable, avoid aggressive batching.
- For throughput-first (background summarization, embedding-style long jobs): larger batching and higher concurrency is fine; aim for GPU occupancy >70%.
- Prefix caching is high ROI for customer templates or reused system prompts; add metric for prefix_cache_hit_rate to Console.
- Kernel selection improvements in runtime are meaningful (10% perf) but don't replace caching/batching tradeoffs.

Action items / follow-ups:
- [ ] Add automated perf test that runs short/medium/long matrix nightly and pushes results to perf-dashboard (JIRA-8722).
- [ ] Add prefix_cache_hit_rate metric to per-model dashboard (work with observability team).
- [ ] Experiment with hybrid batching policy: dynamic thresholding where short seq bypasses batching window if latency-sensitive header flag set. Prototype with perf-client v1.4.\n- [ ] Re-run same matrix with quantization v2 (q8_0) and runtime v0.10 once available.
- [ ] Check memory growth pattern when enabling prefix_cache + BS>8 under heavy concurrency (Noah to run stress test).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to expose batching hints to users without leaking infra details? (suggested: per-route "latency_priority" boolean).
- Can we autosuggest per-route config in Console: recommended batch size + cache toggles based on observed traffic? (tie into Redwood Optimize).

Random notes / scratch numbers (keep for later):
- Token/sec (short-heavy) peak: ~40k tokens/s at BS=16 (but tail too long)
- p99 often 2-3x p95 under load; need to instrument more fine-grained traces to find locking hotspots.

End of scratchpad.

-- Maria
